claims.content: To create and modify system configuration data, including scheduled operations.

goal.raw_text: To create and modify system configuration data, including scheduled operations.

claims.content: System Administrator
The System Administrator must be logged on to the RLCS.
The System Administrator must be authorized to create and modify system configuration data, including scheduled operations.
The System Administrator initiates the configuration of operational schedules to create or modify system configuration data.

trigger.raw_text: The System Administrator initiates the configuration of operational schedules to create or modify system configuration data.

claims.content: The System Administrator accesses the system configuration interface to manage scheduled operations.

The System Administrator creates or modifies a System Operation Command Schedule entry, specifying attributes such as Mode, Start day/time, End day/time, Frequency, and linking it to a System Operational Command ID, Device Command Macro ID, or Device Command ID.
The system validates that the referenced commands (System Operational Command, Device Command Macro, or Device Command) exist and are properly configured in the database entities.

The system stores the updated schedule configuration in the System Operation Command Schedule entity (Entity #36), which can reflect items scheduled to repeat at set periods or entered for immediate execution.
The system logs the configuration change in the System Operation Command Log (Entity #35) to track all modifications for audit purposes.

If the System Administrator attempts to link a non-existent or improperly configured command (System Operational Command, Device Command Macro, or Device Command) to the schedule, the system rejects the entry and prompts for correction.
If the System Administrator is not authorized to modify system configuration data, the system denies access to the scheduling interface.

If the System Administrator enters invalid or incomplete attributes (e.g., missing Mode, Start day/time, End day/time, Frequency, or invalid command linkage) for the System Operation Command Schedule, the system rejects the entry and prompts for correction before allowing resubmission.

If the system encounters a database error while attempting to store or update the System Operation Command Schedule entity (Entity #36), the transaction is rolled back, an error message is displayed to the System Administrator, and the operation is aborted without logging in Entity #35.
If the System Administrator’s session expires or is terminated during schedule configuration, all unsaved changes are discarded, and the user must re-authenticate to resume configuration.

The System Operation Command Schedule entity (Entity #36) is created or updated with valid attributes including Mode, Start day/time, End day/time, Frequency, and a reference to a System Operational Command ID, Device Command Macro ID, or Device Command ID.
The system configuration data for scheduled operations has been successfully modified or created by the authorized System Administrator.
A corresponding entry is recorded in the System Operation Command Log (Entity #35) documenting the date, time, operator, and command details of the schedule configuration change.
The configured schedule may reflect items that repeat at a set period or are entered for immediate execution, as defined in Entity #36 attributes.
